english.title: Possess nuclear material removed from a warehouse with intent to evade prohibition
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly acquired possession of nuclear material which had been unlawfully removed from a

(A)_[warehouse]_
(B)_[Queen's warehouse]_

with intent to evade a

(C)_[prohibition]_
(D)_[restriction]_

relating to the

(E)_[importation]_
(F)_[exportation]_
(G)_[shipment as stores]_

of nuclear material
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(a)(i), (3) and (4C) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
knowingly acquire possession of nuclear material
which has been unlawfully removed
from a warehouse / Queen's warehouse
with intent to evade a prohibition / restriction
relating to the importation / exportation / shipment
as stores of nuclear material

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Any goods in respect of which an offence under this section is committed shall be liable to forfeiture.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a penalty of three times the value of the goods or a fine not exceeding £20,000 whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex

libra.complexpenaltydetails: The maximum financial penalty on summary conviction is three times the value of the goods or a fine not exceeding £20,000 whichever is the greater. Any goods in respect of which an offence under this section is committed shall be liable to forfeiture
